To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can use a model to extract a representation from the observations and actions from a controlled agent, and then use the model in a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to make better decisions in multi-agent settings.

(a) we propose a novel method to learn representations of other agents using encoder-decoder models; (b) we demonstrate that these representations can be used to augment the policy of the controlled agent, which is then trained via deep reinforcement learn- ing; (c) we show that our method achieves signifi- cantly higher performance than baseline methods that do not use learned representations.

(1) our method learns representations about other agents that can be used to improve the performance of the agent that learns the representations, (2) these representations are learned using only the local information of that agent, and (3) these representations can be used to model other agents in cooperative, competitive, and mixed environments, and can be used to train policies in a model-based fashion
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following research question:
How can we learn to model the behaviours of other intelligent agents without access to their local information?

the problem of agent modelling for deep reinforcement learning, and our proposed solution is a novel encoder-decoder architecture which extracts representations from the local observations of a controlled agent.
the problem of learning agent models under partial observability for use in multi-agent deep reinforcement learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented in this work is able to extract useful representations from the local observations of a controlled agent, which are used to augment a decision policy.
our method is a novel approach for modelling the behaviours of other agent's in a multi-agent environment, which is able to achieve higher returns in competitive and mixed multi-agents tasks.

we have developed a new approach to modelling agents in multi-agent reinforcement learning that is able to learn from the local observations and actions of other agents, and then use this information to improve the decision policy of the controlled agent during execution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can learn to model the behaviours of other agent using only partial observability.
we are the first to learn agent representations under partial observability for deep reinforcement learning.

we propose a novel approach for modelling the behaviours of other intelligent agents, which does not require access other agents' information during execution, and is applicable to a wide variety of environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn to model other agents' behaviours without access to their local observations and actions.
it is possible to learn representations about other agents using only the local information of a controlled agent.
the controlled agent can learn to extract representations that are sufficient to understand and model the other agents.
